title: The ground truth remembers the algorithm that drafted it
claim: The final-infarct model is using the ground truth's algorithmic fingerprint — DeepISLES boundary conventions inherited through the 'corrected when needed' annotation pipeline — in the voxels where experts overrode the draft.

title: Does the model bring a vascular map to the scan?
claim: The final-infarct model is using arterial-territory membership — the brain's vascular map — as a spatial prior, producing prediction discontinuities at territory borders between voxels with matched local evidence.

title: The heart's signature in the head scan
claim: The final-infarct model is using systemic contrast transit time — the arm-to-brain bolus delay — as a patient-level severity signal.

title: The model may be watching the patient's eyes
claim: The final-infarct model is using conjugate gaze deviation — the direction the patient's eyes point — as a severity signal when predicting final infarct.

title: The brain's odometer: calcification as the model's age gauge

title: The scan remembers which hospital took it

kill_reason: debate: Reopen idea 027 only if an independently existing, frozen, non-trivially performing final-infarct checkpoint is verified from its executable path to consume both NCCT and CTA voxel intensities; otherwise register the bespoke-model design as a successor.

debate: Obtain an untouched treatment-characterized cohort concretely linked to ISLES'24, a frozen NCCT-inclusive final-infarct model, and temporally aligned hemoglobin, oxygen saturation, acquisition/site, perfusion, reperfusion, and time data sufficient for a preregistered mediation/substitution test.

debate: Obtain the exact archived pre-correction masks and generation provenance, then use a frozen design that isolates training-label exposure while holding acute inputs, cases, architecture, preprocessing, and operating point fixed.

debate: Obtain independently validated acute-space corrected lesion labels that isolate local swelling displacement beyond CSF clipping, then test them in a fully matched training contrast with a localized endpoint.

keystone screen: Per-case occlusion masks and CoW pseudolabels exist, but the release contains no distal-vessel labels, so the distal collateral-reach measure cannot be computed from released files; fresh distal segmentation of the CTA would be a successor idea, not this card.
keystone_evidence: we typically only labelled until the first major bifurcation occurs, and we only labelled the main vessel instead of any minor branches

kill_reason: debate: Obtain a primary-source-validated per-case measurement of functional communicating-artery flow for the same ISLES'24 cases and a design that separates alternate-route redundancy from its downstream hemodynamic consequences.
